claims.exact_statement: For finite capacity M with death rates gamma*n and birth rates in [0,B], the stationary-law frontier min P(N<h) at fixed mean mu=C/gamma is exactly the LP over pi>=0, sum(pi)=1, sum(n*pi_n)=mu, and (n+1)pi_(n+1)<=q*pi_n, q=B/gamma. The feasible means are [0, q Z_(M-1)(q)/Z_M(q)]. Every LP vertex has prefix support {0,...,K} and at most one strict birth-cap edge within that positive support; therefore some optimizer has all supported birth rates at B except for at most one interior rate, followed by a support cutoff.
assumptions: time-homogeneous state-feedback rates lambda_n in [0,B] for n<M and lambda_M=0
independent per-molecule death at rate gamma
claims.status: internally reconstructed proof; novelty and priority unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: General constrained average CTMDP LP is established prior art; the specialized adjacent-ratio reduction and one-partial-edge extreme-point statement were not found in the limited source scan. Exact assumption mapping to Guo-Huang-Song 2012 remains UNKNOWN.
claims.costs: Stationary translation events per unit time C=gamma*mu; mean abundance mu; hard rate cap B; capacity M. Circuit sensing, implementation, promoter-state, delay, growth, and ATP costs are uncharged. Finite candidate enumeration has O(M^2) candidates and O(M) rate-table output, with rational bit growth additional.
claims.falsifier: A feasible finite LP vertex with two strict edges before its positive-support cutoff, or a feasible stationary law outside the adjacent-ratio polytope, refutes the theorem.
claims.next_gate: Map the theorem against the full assumptions and controlled birth-death example in Guo-Huang-Song 2012 and search specifically for the same fixed-mean tail objective or one-partial-edge structure.

claims.exact_statement: With gamma=1, B=1/2, M=2, h=2, and C=mu=1/64, the exact sharp failure probability is 383/384, attained by stationary pi=(379,4,1)/384 and rates lambda=(4/379,1/2,0). Every standard single-cutoff policy with the same fixed mean has failure probability 1. Thus upper-cutoff threshold policies are not generally optimal for the fixed-mean low-tail objective.
assumptions: same finite-capacity birth-death interface as C2-FINITE-LP-VERTEX
standard cutoff means lambda_n=B below cutoff, at most one partial cutoff rate, then zero above
claims.status: exact rational counterexample and sharp M=2 instance; script checked
claims.novelty_boundary: The counterexample is an exact consequence of the model and is not a priority claim; threshold optimality is known for other queue objectives and those hypotheses/objectives differ.
claims.costs: Translation rate C=1/64 per time unit; mean count 1/64. Selected law E[N^2]=1/48 and Var(N)=253/12288. The matched cutoff law E[N^2]=1/64 and Var(N)=63/4096, confirming the reliability objective is not variance minimization.
claims.falsifier: An exact feasible single-cutoff rate table at mean 1/64 with P(N<2)<1 would refute the comparator claim.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether a measured, realizable promoter/translation family can implement the nonmonotone rate shape (low basal leak, saturated rate after seeding, cutoff) and retain any reliability advantage.

claims.exact_statement: For countably infinite capacity and finite q=B/gamma, the stationary-law LP with the same adjacent inequalities and a fixed finite mean mu is compact in l1, its lower-tail minimum is attained, the feasible mean interval is [0,q], and an extreme optimizer can be chosen with either finite prefix support and at most one strict supported edge before its cutoff, or infinite support with at most one strict edge total.
assumptions: time-homogeneous state-feedback rates bounded by B
claims.status: internally reconstructed proof using factorial domination, compactness, and a three-block perturbation; external validation and novelty unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The immigration-death Poisson dominator is established sampling prior art for bounded Markov reaction propensities. This result optimizes a fixed-mean tail and derives an LP extreme-point structure; novelty not established.
claims.costs: Average translations C=gamma*mu; no finite truncation error is introduced in the mathematical statement. Numerical evaluation of the countable candidate minimum needs certified tail control and is not implemented.
claims.falsifier: A feasible infinite-mean law violating pi_n<=q^n/n!, or a proof that the feasible set is not compact under the stated topology, invalidates the compactness argument.
claims.next_gate: Independently verify the infinite-dimensional extreme-point argument and derive a finite truncation/error certificate for evaluating its countable candidate family.
